    25→Main API of the ssh application
    26→
    27→This is the interface module for the `SSH` application. The Secure Shell (SSH)
    28→Protocol is a protocol for secure remote login and other secure network services
    29→over an insecure network. See [ssh](ssh_app.md#supported) for details of
    30→supported RFCs, versions, algorithms and unicode handling.
    31→
    32→With the SSH application it is possible to start _clients_ and to start
    33→_daemons_ (servers).
    34→
    35→Clients are started with `connect/2`, `connect/3` or `connect/4`. They open an
    36→encrypted connection on top of TCP/IP. In that encrypted connection one or more
    37→channels could be opened with
    38→[ssh_connection:session_channel/2,4](`ssh_connection:session_channel/2`).
    39→
    40→Each channel is an isolated "pipe" between a client-side process and a
    41→server-side process. Those process pairs could handle for example file transfers
    42→(sftp) or remote command execution (shell, exec and/or cli). If a custom shell
    43→is implemented, the user of the client could execute the special commands
    44→remotely. Note that the user is not necessarily a human but probably a system
    45→interfacing the SSH app.
    46→
    47→A server-side subssystem (channel) server is requested by the client with
    48→`ssh_connection:subsystem/4`.
    49→
    50→A server (daemon) is started with [daemon/1](`daemon/2`), `daemon/2` or
    51→[daemon/3](`daemon/2`). Possible channel handlers (subsystems) are declared with
    52→the [subsystem](`t:subsystem_daemon_option/0`) option when the daemon is
    53→started.
    54→
    55→To just run a shell on a remote machine, there are functions that bundles the
    56→needed three steps needed into one: [shell/1,2,3](`shell/1`). Similarly, to just
    57→open an sftp (file transfer) connection to a remote machine, the simplest way is
    58→to use [ssh_sftp:start_channel/1,2,3](`ssh_sftp:start_channel/1`).
    59→
    60→To write your own client channel handler, use the behaviour
    61→`m:ssh_client_channel`. For server channel handlers use `m:ssh_server_channel`
    62→behaviour (replaces ssh_daemon_channel).
    63→
    64→Both clients and daemons accept options that control the exact behaviour. Some
    65→options are common to both. The three sets are called
    66→[Client Options](`t:client_options/0`), [Daemon Options](`t:daemon_options/0`)
    67→and [Common Options](`t:common_options/0`).
    68→
    69→The descriptions of the options uses the
    70→[Erlang Type Language](`e:system:typespec.md`) with explaining text.

    72→> #### Note {: .info }

    76→## Keys and files

    78→A number of objects must be present for the SSH application to work. Those
    79→objects are per default stored in files. The default names, paths and file

    81→generated with the `ssh-keygen` program from OpenSSH. See the
    82→[User's Guide](using_ssh.md#running-an-erlang-ssh-daemon).

    85→[`user_dir`](`t:ssh_file:user_dir_common_option/0`) and
    86→[`system_dir`](`t:ssh_file:system_dir_daemon_option/0`).

    22→The ssh application implements the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol and provides an

    24→
    25→## Description
    26→
    27→The `ssh` application is an implementation of the SSH protocol in Erlang. `ssh`
    28→offers API functions to write customized SSH clients and servers as well as
    29→making the Erlang shell available over SSH. An SFTP client, `ssh_sftp`, and
    30→server, `ssh_sftpd`, are also included.

    32→## Dependencies
    33→
    34→The `ssh` application uses the applications `m:public_key` and `m:crypto` to
    35→handle public keys and encryption. Hence, these applications must be loaded for
    36→the `ssh` application to work. The call `ssh:start/0` will do the necessary
    37→calls to [application:start/1,2](`application:start/1`) before it starts the
    38→`ssh` itself.

    40→## Configuration
    41→
    42→The SSH application uses Configuration Parameters. Where to set them are
    43→described in [config User's Guide](`e:kernel:config.md`) with SSH details in
    44→[Configuration in SSH](configurations.md).
    45→
    46→Some special configuration files from OpenSSH are also used:
    47→
    48→- `known_hosts`
    49→- `authorized_keys`
    50→- `authorized_keys2`
    51→- `id_dsa` _(supported but disabled by default)_
